questions.question: What do the old and new leaflets differ on?
questions.explanation: 新舊傳單對警鈴測試指示有所不同。

questions.question: What does the older leaflet prove?
options: The alarm failed on flood night
questions.explanation: 舊傳單只能證明指示曾存在。

paragraphs.en: The troupe held a reading for invited witnesses and community members. On each seat lay a simple notice: anyone could ask to stop a scene using their own words. Mara opened by explaining which parts were verified, which were memories, and which were invented for the stage.
paragraphs.zh: 劇團為受訪者與社區居民舉辦讀劇。每個座位都放著簡單告示：任何人都可以要求停止使用自己說過的話。瑪拉開場說明哪些來自文件、哪些是回憶、哪些是戲劇創作。

paragraphs.en: One resident stopped Mara in the hall to thank her for leaving a question unanswered. As a child, he had watched adults argue about the flood without listening to one another. The scene gave him a way to remember the disagreement without choosing a side for his parents.
paragraphs.zh: 一位居民在走廊攔住瑪拉，感謝她沒有硬給問題答案。他小時候看著大人為水災爭吵，卻不願互相聽。這場戲讓他得以記得分歧，而不必替父母選邊。

paragraphs.en: Ada listened to Nia read the river-gate scene. She corrected one time and asked to remove the detail about her daughter's school. Mara marked the changes in full view of the audience. The revision was not an embarrassment; it was the point of the meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 艾達聽妮雅讀水閘那場戲，更正了一個時間，並要求刪去女兒就讀學校的細節。瑪拉當眾標記修改。這些修正不是丟臉的事，而正是會議的目的。

paragraphs.en: Afterward the stage crew would prepare a parade for the local heritage festival. A clown greeted visitors beside a wooden bull. A photographer carried a camera, and a woman found a lost purse near the ticket desk. A deposit box held the returned items until their owners could be identified. A workshop displayed countable pieces of wheat bread and asked children to stitch a line across fabric. The chairs looked hollow underneath, so a worker checked each one. Mara used a marker to draw a zone where the audience should not stand. The first note of the original song seemed to awaken an old memory in many people. At the end a young singer said, “I want a truthful program, not a fight.” The reaction was quiet and stronger than cheers. The chair approved the next steps but refused to rush the conclusion. The chair said she could approve the listening plan but could not approve a result before seeing every document. Technicians might detect a matching sound, yet the board still had to decide what that match proved. Mara found that distinction useful; it protected the careful work of the listeners and the writers alike. The invited performance tested whether the script respected witnesses rather than promising more ticket sales.
paragraphs.zh: 會後舞台團隊要準備地方文化節遊行。小丑在木製公牛旁迎接訪客。攝影師拿著相機，一名女子在售票桌附近找到遺失的錢包。失物先放在押物箱，等確認主人。工作坊展示能逐塊計數的小麥麵包，並教孩子在布上縫一條線。椅子底部似乎中空，員工逐張檢查。瑪拉用記號筆畫出觀眾不得站立的區域。原始歌曲的第一個音符似乎喚醒許多人的舊記憶。結束後一名小歌手說：「我想要真實的節目單，不想吵架。」反應安靜，力量卻比歡呼還大。主席核准下一步程序，拒絕倉促下結論。 主席說她可以核准試聽計畫，卻不能在看完文件前預先核准結果。技師或許能偵測相符聲音，委員會仍須決定相符究竟證明什麼。瑪拉覺得這種區分有用，因為它同時保護聽眾與作者仔細完成的工作。這場受邀觀眾參加的演出，是檢驗劇本有沒有尊重證人，而不是承諾賣出更多門票。

paragraphs.en: Mara collected the written comments in a box with a clear label and a closing date. Participants could take their own notes back before the next version was shared. She did not promise to use every suggestion. She promised to read each one and explain major decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉把書面意見放進標示清楚、附截止日的箱子。下一版分享前，參與者可以取回自己的意見。她沒有保證採用每個建議，只承諾逐一閱讀，並說明重要決定。

paragraphs.en: A man in the audience argued that sponsors should be thanked, not questioned. Another audience member asked why the play could not do both. Mara accepted the question and said the next draft would distinguish useful repairs from unanswered safety decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 一名觀眾說應該感謝贊助商，不該質疑；另一人問為何不能同時做到。瑪拉接受這個問題，說下版會區分實際有用的修復與仍待回答的安全決策。

paragraphs.en: One comment asked whether the mother's silence after the last question meant forgiveness. Nia tried the pause in two ways: first looking down, then looking directly toward the imaginary official. The words remained identical, but the second version held the question open. Mara asked Ada which movement resembled the decision she had described. Ada chose the direct look. June recorded it as an agreed performance choice rather than a new historical fact. The reading had uncovered a meaning hidden in an actor's eyes, beyond anything a permission form could explain alone.
paragraphs.zh: 一則意見問，母親問完後沉默，是否表示原諒。妮雅試了兩種停頓：先低頭，再直視想像中的官員。文字完全相同，第二種卻讓問題繼續存在。瑪拉問艾達，哪個動作接近她曾描述的決定。艾達選擇直視。君把它記成同意的表演選擇，而非新的歷史事實。這次讀劇找出藏在眼神裡的意思，單靠授權表無法說清。

paragraphs.en: After the guests left, Nia said that the audience had not made the play weaker. They had made it belong to its subject without taking it away from the writer. Mara finally believed that a revision could be an act of respect.
paragraphs.zh: 客人離開後，妮雅說觀眾沒有讓戲變弱，而是讓故事真正屬於其主題，同時不剝奪創作者的工作。瑪拉終於相信，修改也能是一種尊重。

questions.question: Who requests removal of a school detail?
questions.explanation: 艾達要求刪去女兒就讀學校的資訊。

questions.question: What does the new reading invite?
questions.explanation: 讀劇讓當事人有機會更正內容。

title: The Contract With One False Sentence

paragraphs.en: The revised sponsor contract arrived with one sentence highlighted: all interview subjects had approved the sponsor's final text. Mara had the list of actual permissions in front of her. Several people had approved only specific sections; Rina had withdrawn entirely.
paragraphs.zh: 新贊助合約有一句話被標亮：「所有受訪者都同意贊助商最後版本。」瑪拉手上有真正的授權清單：多人只同意特定片段，莉娜更已完全撤回。

paragraphs.en: The contract lay on Mara's desk long after she had returned it. She made a note of the sentence she could not sign and the reasons for refusing. She wanted future company members to understand that the decision was based on actual permissions, not a personal fight with a wealthy man.
paragraphs.zh: 合約退回後，那句話仍在瑪拉腦中。她記下不能簽的句子與拒絕理由，希望未來團員明白：這項決定依據真實授權，不是與一位有錢人的私人爭執。

paragraphs.en: Mara drew a line through that sentence and sent the document back without signing it. Celeste worried that this would destroy their final chance at funding. Mara answered that saving a theatre by making a false statement would create a different kind of loss.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉劃掉那句話，將合約退回而不簽署。席莉絲擔心這會毀掉最後資金機會。瑪拉說，若靠虛假聲明保住劇院，只會造成另一種失去。

paragraphs.en: The notice arrived at dawn after an ambulance passed the office. Outside, a farmer led cattle along a road near the dam. The air was cold enough to show each breath. A technician explained that the replacement copy on a disk would be stored with a printed log. A dishonest correction would be worse than the first error, so every step needed review. Mara did not dislike Vale’s musicians, who had worked hard on the arrangement. A handyman carried a handy tool kit while a team went farther down the hall. One visitor wore a monk’s robe for a cultural event, another carried a magnet for a science class. A clerk checked the stable storage shelf and marked the territory where records must be kept. Though the decision was tough for the festival, the written notice quoted the first verse correctly. Mara noticed that it did not omit Celeste’s recommendation about two approvals. The board had taken the practical lesson seriously. The kitchen staff were preparing shrimp for lunch, and a cook asked children not to scatter their papers near the food. Mara moved the document table to a clean corner before discussing the decision.
paragraphs.zh: 通知在清晨送達，當時一輛救護車正經過辦公室。外面農夫牽牛群走過水壩附近道路，空氣冷得能看見每口呼吸。技師說明替換檔案會存於光碟，另附紙本紀錄。若更正不誠實，就會比最初錯誤更糟，因此每一步都需審核。瑪拉並不討厭韋爾的樂手，他們確實努力編曲。修理工提著方便的工具組，其他工作人員往走廊更遠處走。一位參訪者穿著僧袍參加文化活動，另一人為科學課帶著磁鐵。職員檢查穩固的儲存架，標出紀錄必須保存的區域。即使決定對音樂節很艱難，書面公告仍正確引用原歌第一節。瑪拉注意到，決定沒有漏掉席莉絲提出的雙重核准建議。委員會認真看待這個實務教訓。 廚房人員正在準備午餐的蝦子，廚師請孩子不要把紙張散落在食物附近。瑪拉先把文件桌移到乾淨角落，再討論決定。

paragraphs.en: June worked out how many seats the smaller show could use without crowding the exits. The income would be modest, but the figures were visible to everyone. Mara liked the honest numbers more than a grand promise whose hidden price was another person's silence.
paragraphs.zh: 君算出小型演出在不阻塞出口下能使用的座位數。收入不多，但每個數字都公開。瑪拉寧願接受誠實的數字，也不要一項以別人沉默為暗中代價的豪華承諾。

paragraphs.en: June prepared a public budget for a smaller show. The company could borrow chairs, lower advertising costs, and charge a modest optional ticket price. None of those choices was pleasant, but they were decisions the team could discuss openly.
paragraphs.zh: 君準備小規模演出的公開預算。劇團可以借椅子、減少廣告支出，並採用低額自願票價。這些選擇不輕鬆，卻都能讓團隊公開討論。

paragraphs.en: Mara asked the office manager to acknowledge receipt of the unsigned contract. She wanted the record to show refusal, not a document accidentally overlooked before a deadline. The manager returned a short confirmation. June attached the approved budget beneath it and asked the cast to choose which expenses could wait. They kept transport for older witnesses and removed a decorative banner. Theo offered no heroic promise. He simply confirmed the equipment he could supply within his agreed hours. For once the plan on paper described the resources they really had.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉請辦公室經理確認收到未簽的合約，好讓紀錄顯示這是拒絕，而不是錯過期限的疏忽。經理回覆簡短確認。君把核准的預算附在下面，請演員選擇哪些支出能延後。他們保留年長證人的交通費，刪去裝飾布條。提歐沒有英雄式承諾，只確認約定工時內能提供的設備。紙上的計畫這次確實對應他們擁有的資源。

paragraphs.en: Theo told Mara that he admired her choice but did not want to be treated as the person who had rescued her. Mara smiled. She said she was hoping he might become someone she could argue with and still want to see tomorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 提歐說他欣賞她的選擇，卻不希望被當成救她的人。瑪拉笑著說，她希望他成為一個即使爭辯過，隔天仍想見面的人。

questions.question: What does Mara refuse to sign?
questions.explanation: 瑪拉拒絕簽署不實的全面授權聲明。

questions.question: What does the team make public instead?
questions.explanation: 團隊公開較小規模的預算。

paragraphs.en: The theatre board opened a public review, with seats reserved for workers, residents, and interview participants. Mara presented the three script editions and explained how they had been kept. She did not ask the board to punish a person before examining the evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 劇院董事會展開公開審查，為員工、居民與受訪者保留座位。瑪拉提出三個劇本版本，說明保存過程。她沒有要求董事會在查證前先懲罰任何人。

paragraphs.en: Mara placed the untouched drafts on a stand so the board could see their dates without turning pages during testimony. Her hands shook as she began to speak. She did not disguise the feeling. She read the first sentence slowly and let the evidence, rather than her anger, guide the rest.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉把未改動的原稿放在架上，讓董事會能看到日期，不必在作證時來回翻頁。開口時她的手顫抖，卻沒有掩飾。她慢慢讀出第一句，讓證據而非憤怒帶領後面的說明。

paragraphs.en: June described the blue pencil notes and admitted she should have signed them. Nia explained why she had refused the unapproved scene. Ada said she had chosen which words could be used and valued having that choice respected.
paragraphs.zh: 君說明藍鉛筆註記，承認自己應署名。妮雅解釋為何拒演未授權場景。艾達說，她自己決定哪些話能被使用，也重視這項選擇受到尊重。

paragraphs.en: Someone had placed a model bomb in the history exhibit, clearly marked as a harmless prop. A worker wiped dust from the shelf while a small moth moved toward the light. Near the café, a child pressed a thumb against a stamp pad and left a bright mark. The poster warned about pollution and asked visitors to wrap food instead of leaving waste. A baker complained that good bread was scarce and that the oven had spoiled the morning batch. A religious choir rehearsed in the next room. A teacher drew a minus sign and explained that a successful strategy should not take something away from one group merely to reward another. June put a marker beside the voting sheet so nobody would have to crawl under the table to find a pen. Mara touched her cheek and smiled at the hint of hope in the room. The point was to get rid of confusion, not to make the loudest side win. “This is not a pure contest between good and bad people,” Mara told the voters. “A rushed plan could spoil the concert even when our reasons are good.” A notice for the next board election hung by the door, reminding everyone that leaders could be questioned too.
paragraphs.zh: 歷史展櫃裡有人放了模型炸彈，清楚標註是無害道具。工人擦掉架上灰塵，小飛蛾往燈光飛去。咖啡館旁孩子用拇指按在印泥墊上，留下鮮明記號。海報提醒大家注意污染，請訪客包好食物、勿亂丟垃圾。麵包師抱怨好麵包稀缺，烤箱還弄壞了早上那批。隔壁宗教合唱團正在練習。老師畫出減號，解釋成功策略不該為獎勵一群人而剝奪另一群人的東西。君把記號筆放在投票單旁，免得有人得鑽到桌下找筆。瑪拉摸摸臉頰，對房間裡一絲希望微笑。重點是擺脫混亂，不是讓最大聲的人獲勝。 「這不是善與惡之間純粹的競賽，」瑪拉對投票者說，「即使出發點好，匆忙計畫仍可能毀掉音樂會。」門旁貼著下一次董事會選舉公告，提醒大家領導者也應接受提問。

paragraphs.en: A worker asked if the review meant that everyone who had followed Celeste's instructions would be blamed. Mara answered that responsibility needed to be considered one decision at a time. She asked the board to keep paying completed work while it examined who had approved the edits.
paragraphs.zh: 一位員工問審查是否代表所有遵照席莉絲指示的人都會被責怪。瑪拉說，責任必須逐項決定檢視。她請董事會在調查誰核准改稿時，仍支付已完成的工作。

paragraphs.en: The office manager confirmed the print record and file dates. The board chair asked Mara whether the records proved an order from the sponsor. Mara said they did not. She repeated only the parts she could demonstrate.
paragraphs.zh: 辦公室經理確認列印紀錄與檔案日期。主席問這是否證明贊助商下令改稿。瑪拉回答不能，只重述她能佐證的部分。

paragraphs.en: A board member asked Mara to summarize the entire dispute in a single sentence. Mara tried, then asked permission to use three. The blue marks raised consent concerns; the black cuts changed the public question; the financing proposal sought approval that had never been given. Collapsing those points would erase the very distinction her inquiry had uncovered. The chair allowed the longer answer. At the back of the room, June opened her clenched hand. She could finally hear her own warning described without being made responsible for somebody else's deletion.
paragraphs.zh: 一位董事請瑪拉用一句話概括爭議。她試了，隨後請求用三句：藍記號提出授權疑慮，黑刪改改變公共問題，資金提案則要求從未取得的全面同意。把三者壓成一句，會抹去調查才釐清的區別。主席准許較長回答。後排的君鬆開握緊的手。她終於聽見自己的提醒被準確說明，不必替別人的刪改負責。

paragraphs.en: As the meeting ended for the day, Celeste requested time to speak at the next session. She looked tired but did not ask Mara to withdraw the case. The board agreed to hear her statement without promising any particular result.
paragraphs.zh: 當天會議結束前，席莉絲要求在下一場發言。她看來疲憊，卻沒有要求瑪拉撤案。董事會同意聽她說明，不預先承諾任何結果。

questions.question: Who openly explains the blue notes at the hearing?
questions.explanation: 君公開說明藍鉛筆註記來源。

questions.question: What does Mara say the print records do not prove?
questions.explanation: 瑪拉承認列印紀錄無法證明贊助商下令。

paragraphs.en: Celeste told the board that she had combined June's comments with sponsor requests in one new script. She admitted making the black-square cuts and failing to tell the cast. The sponsor had suggested avoiding the company name, but Celeste herself had chosen the words and approved printing.
paragraphs.zh: 席莉絲向董事會表示，自己把君的提醒與贊助商要求合併成新稿。她承認做了黑方塊刪改，卻未告知演員。贊助商曾建議避開公司名稱，但選字與批准列印的人是她自己。

paragraphs.en: Celeste described her fear without asking for it to be called an excuse. She said she had once believed a director must carry every risk alone, even when that meant hiding a difficult choice. Mara answered that shared responsibility could feel slower but would leave fewer people unheard.
paragraphs.zh: 席莉絲說出恐懼，卻沒有要求大家把它當成藉口。她曾以為導演必須獨自承擔所有風險，即使因此隱瞞艱難選擇。瑪拉回答，共同負責也許比較慢，卻能讓更少的人被忽視。

paragraphs.en: The board asked why she had hidden that responsibility. Celeste answered that she feared losing the theatre and the jobs around it. Mara did not call the fear imaginary. She asked Celeste to acknowledge that the change had also removed a question residents deserved to hear.
paragraphs.zh: 董事會問她為何隱瞞責任。席莉絲說，她害怕失去劇院與相關工作。瑪拉沒有說這種恐懼是假的，只請她承認修改也刪去了居民理應聽見的問題。

paragraphs.en: An adventure story was being read beneath a tree outside the office. The storyteller used a thin cord to bind two books, and a cricket chirped beside a little donkey. A child raised a fist in play while another found a coat hanger. Across the courtyard, a health class discussed kidney care and why health advice required experts. A costumed lord from a theatre group bowed to passersby. Meanwhile, visitors attended an oral history talk about the presence of local musicians in the town. The speaker said that proof must be clear and a demand reasonable. Mara had reserved a seat in the shallow end of the hall because she did not want to block the door. A student held a tablet, teased a friend about the spelling of a song title, and tossed a ball into a box. The adviser smiled and called the spelling issue tricky but easy to fix. The legal words on Mara’s page were harder, yet careful reading made them less frightening. The adviser said it was wise to reserve time for questions before signing. The children could tease one another during rehearsal or toss a soft ball outside, but nobody should treat legal terms like a game.
paragraphs.zh: 辦公室外的樹下有人講冒險故事。說書人用細繩綁起兩本書，蟋蟀在小驢子旁鳴叫。一個孩子玩耍時舉起拳頭，另一個找到衣架。庭院另一頭健康課討論腎臟保健，以及為何醫療建議需要專家。劇團扮成領主的演員向路人鞠躬。與此同時，訪客聽地方音樂家的口述歷史。講者說證據必須清楚，要求也要合理。瑪拉預留靠大廳較淺處的座位，不想擋門。學生拿著平板，取笑朋友拼錯歌名，又把球拋進箱子。顧問笑說拼字問題有點棘手，但容易修正。瑪拉頁上的法律用字更難，仔細讀卻讓它不再那麼可怕。 顧問說簽名前保留提問時間是明智的。孩子可在排練時互相打趣，或在外頭拋軟球，但沒人應把法律條款當遊戲。

paragraphs.en: After the admission, Nia asked Celeste whether she could work with the company again. Celeste did not request forgiveness in return for answering. She said she would accept whatever limits the board set. Mara thought that taking responsibility meant letting other people decide what trust could be rebuilt.
paragraphs.zh: 承認之後，妮雅問席莉絲未來是否還能合作。席莉絲沒有要求對方因自己回答就原諒她，只說會接受董事會的限制。瑪拉想，負責任也包括讓別人決定信任能重建多少。

paragraphs.en: Celeste agreed to correct the editorial record and to stop claiming that all witnesses had approved the script. She also asked the board to keep paying the workers who had done their jobs honestly. The chair promised to consider that separately.
paragraphs.zh: 席莉絲同意更正編輯紀錄，不再宣稱所有受訪者都同意劇本，也請董事會繼續支付認真工作的員工薪水。主席承諾分開處理。

paragraphs.en: The chair asked Celeste what she would do differently if a future sponsor objected to a line. Celeste began to answer that she would consult Mara, then stopped. She added the performers and any interview participant whose permission might change. June would record the proposal before a decision, rather than receiving a finished script afterward. Mara listened for the order of those steps. The difference was practical: people needed to be present while a choice remained open. A corrected record of the past would matter more if it changed tomorrow's rehearsal.
paragraphs.zh: 主席問席莉絲，未來若贊助商反對台詞，她會如何處理。席莉絲先說要詢問瑪拉，接著停下，補上演員，以及授權可能受影響的受訪者。君應在決定前記錄提案，而不是事後才收到完成的劇本。瑪拉仔細聽步驟順序。差異很實際：選擇尚未定案時，相關的人就應在場。更正過去的紀錄，若能改變明日排練，才更有意義。

paragraphs.en: Mara left the hearing without celebrating. The case had not revealed a simple monster. It had revealed choices made under pressure and a system that allowed one director to change a community story without telling its people.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉離開聽證時沒有慶祝。案件沒有找出簡單的怪物，而是揭開人們在壓力下的選擇，以及一個容許導演不告知當事人就改寫社區故事的制度。

questions.question: What does Celeste acknowledge?
questions.explanation: 席莉絲承認黑方塊刪改是自己所做。

questions.question: What does Celeste agree to correct?
questions.explanation: 董事會要求更正編輯紀錄與相關程序。

paragraphs.en: The board voted to reject the false statement in the sponsor contract and to suspend the edited performance copy. It approved a smaller independent show on the condition that permissions, safety, and final changes were listed publicly.
paragraphs.zh: 董事會表決拒絕贊助合約中的錯誤聲明，暫停使用被改動的演出稿；同時有條件同意小型獨立演出，要求公開列示授權、安全措施與最後修改。

paragraphs.en: June pinned the new editing rules to a board beside the rehearsal schedule. Every proposed change would name its author, its reason, and the permissions it affected. Anyone could ask for a review of a change without being called difficult. Mara offered to test the rules on her next draft first.
paragraphs.zh: 君把新的編輯規則貼在排練表旁。每項修改都要註明作者、理由與受影響的授權，任何人都可要求複查而不被說成難搞。瑪拉主動提出，讓這些規則先用在自己的下一版。

paragraphs.en: Celeste offered her resignation. The board asked her to stay for a limited transition so that staff payments and stage records could be completed, with another person supervising her editorial work. Mara said accountability required clear tasks, not only a dramatic exit.
paragraphs.zh: 席莉絲提出辭職。董事會請她留任有限的交接期，完成薪資和舞台紀錄，並由他人監督編輯工作。瑪拉說，負責任需要清楚工作，而不只是戲劇性的離開。

paragraphs.en: The local adviser showed her a poster from a school concert. A toy jeep stood outside a museum, and a koala picture decorated the children’s room. At a pub across the street, somebody began to hum an old tune. A sun ray crossed the grassy square, where visitors were warned not to step onto the garden. A child made a loud bang by dropping a box, and a teacher asked whether the sound was scary. Mara said it was sensible to check before assuming danger. The music on the old poster had been a constant part of her childhood. She had hesitated then to sing in public; now she could trace the path from one school hall to the festival stage. The museum also displayed goods that the town used to import. Mrs. Chen wiped a table with a napkin and smiled at Mara’s quiet pride. Her old teacher said fame could become bait if someone chased glory instead of useful work. “Music may help a person heal, but do not hesitate to ask for real support when you need it,” she added. Mara thanked her. The independent show would take place in Mara's hometown, but she refused to use local people as decoration.
paragraphs.zh: 地方顧問拿出學校音樂會舊海報。博物館外有玩具吉普車，兒童室掛著無尾熊圖片。街對面的酒館有人哼唱老曲調。陽光射線越過長滿草的小廣場，警示牌提醒訪客別踏進花園。孩子讓箱子砰地落地，老師問聲音是否可怕。瑪拉說先檢查再判斷危險是明智的。舊海報上的音樂是她童年恆久的一部分。那時她還會猶豫要不要公開演唱；如今她能追溯從學校禮堂走到音樂節舞台的路。博物館也展示小鎮以前進口的貨物。陳老師用餐巾擦桌，對瑪拉安靜的自豪微笑。 老老師說，若追逐榮耀而不再重視有用工作，名氣就會變成誘餌。「音樂也許能幫助人療癒，但真正需要支援時不要猶豫求助，」她補充。瑪拉向她道謝。獨立演出將在瑪拉的家鄉舉行，但她拒絕把在地居民當成裝飾背景。

paragraphs.en: As the company packed its old costumes, Mara found the first blank page that had started the inquiry. She did not throw it away. She put it in a folder marked 'Why we changed the process.' It no longer represented only an insult to her writing; it marked a lesson she had helped earn.
paragraphs.zh: 劇團整理舊服裝時，瑪拉找到當初引發調查的那張空白頁。她沒有丟掉，而是放入標為「我們為何改變程序」的資料夾。它不再只是對作品的冒犯，也記錄了她參與學會的一課。

paragraphs.en: June received permission to publish a version history showing who had made each change and why. Witness names were replaced with codes where needed. Nia agreed to perform, and Theo would lead one final technical safety check.
paragraphs.zh: 君獲准公布版本歷程，標示誰在何時、為何修改，必要時以代號保護證人。妮雅答應演出，提歐則負責最後一次技術安全檢查。

paragraphs.en: The first change under the new rules came from Mara herself. She wanted to shorten a transition before the final speech. June asked which approved words would be affected. Mara almost said it was only a small cut, then brought out the marked page. Together they found a phrase that belonged to Ada's chosen account. Mara sent the revised passage for review before rehearsal. The delay was inconvenient and useful. A rule written to limit Celeste would have been hollow if the playwright expected an exception whenever her own deadline became tight.
paragraphs.zh: 新規則下第一項修改來自瑪拉自己：她想縮短最後演說前的過場。君問會影響哪些已獲准的文字。瑪拉差點說只是小刪節，隨後拿出標記頁。兩人發現其中一句屬於艾達選定的敘述。瑪拉在排練前送出新版供核對。等待既不方便，也有用。若劇作家每逢趕稿就要求例外，那條用來限制席莉絲的規則便失去意義。

paragraphs.en: Mara walked through the now quieter theatre and recognized the difference between owning her writing and owning every voice within it. She could protect her words while allowing other people to choose what happened to theirs.
paragraphs.zh: 瑪拉走過安靜許多的劇院，終於分清楚：擁有自己的作品，不代表擁有作品中每一個人的聲音。她可以捍衛自己的文字，也尊重他人決定自己的話如何被使用。

questions.question: What does the board approve?
questions.explanation: 董事會准許有條件進行小型獨立演出。

questions.question: What must be listed for the show?
questions.explanation: 演出須列明授權、安全與最後變更。

paragraphs.en: Rain arrived on the afternoon of the final outdoor rehearsal. June moved the cast into a covered school hall under the backup plan agreed by the board. Nobody improvised an unsafe move merely to keep the dramatic view of the river.
paragraphs.zh: 最後一次戶外彩排當天下午下起雨。君依照董事會核准的備案，把演員移到有屋頂的學校禮堂。沒有人為了保留戲劇性的河景而冒險移動。

paragraphs.en: Rain beat on the school hall windows while June checked the backup seats. The actors seemed disappointed at first, but the covered room let everyone hear the words more clearly. Mara said the river did not need to appear as real water. It needed to be present in the questions the characters asked.
paragraphs.zh: 雨打在學校禮堂窗上，君檢查備用座位。演員起初失望，但有屋頂的房間反而讓每句台詞更清楚。瑪拉說，河不必以真水出現，只要存在於角色提出的問題裡。

paragraphs.en: Theo tested each borrowed lamp with the school caretaker. Mara checked that the printed program listed sources and clearly marked invented dialogue. Nia tried the mother's final scene without music and discovered that a pause could carry the whole room.
paragraphs.zh: 提歐和學校管理員逐一測試借來的燈。瑪拉檢查節目單是否列明資料來源並標示虛構對話。妮雅不配樂地試演母親最後一幕，發現一段停頓就能撐住整個空間。

paragraphs.en: An airline advertisement hung beside the hall, offering flights to distant cities. A cheerful student wore a bicycle helmet while delivering posters in the chilly morning. A police officer helped manage traffic after an arrest nearby, and the organiser warned everyone not to follow rumors. Behind the hall a vehicle carried benches from a vacant lot. Someone used an old rag to clean the keys of the piano. A young performer said she did not dare sing alone; another feared becoming the loser in a music contest. Mara explained that the community concert would not rank talent. Nobody had to suffer for failing a test. The group would promote careful listening, not competition. A radio from the river dock reported that the navy would hold a public safety display, and a travel film showed a jungle far away. These events were not part of the concert, but the neighborhood was alive with many different stories. The organizer warned that a careless attitude toward cables could be harmful. Theo gave a tired sigh, then asked every helper to warn him immediately if a wire felt hot or loose. Nobody laughed at the safety rule.
paragraphs.zh: 禮堂旁掛著航空公司廣告，宣傳飛往遠方城市的航班。清晨寒冷，一位開朗學生戴著自行車安全帽送海報。附近發生逮捕事件，警員協助疏導交通；主辦者提醒大家不要跟著傳聞走。禮堂後方有車輛從空地運來長椅。有人用舊抹布擦鋼琴琴鍵。一名小歌手說自己不敢獨唱，另一人怕在音樂比賽變成輸家。瑪拉解釋這場社區演唱會不排名天分，也沒人需要為測驗失利而受苦。大家要推廣仔細傾聽，而不是競爭。河邊碼頭的收音機報導海軍即將舉辦公共安全展示，旅遊影片則介紹遠方叢林。這些活動都與音樂會無關，卻顯示社區有許多不同故事。 主辦者警告，對電線抱持隨便態度可能有害。提歐疲倦地嘆口氣，接著請每位幫手只要發現電線發熱或鬆脫就立刻警告他。沒有人嘲笑這條安全規定。

paragraphs.en: Before the doors opened, a visitor asked June whether the sponsor's seats were reserved. June showed the seating plan: places were held for access needs and invited participants, with no private block for the former sponsor. She offered the visitor the same available seat as everyone else. Mara overheard and resisted the urge to turn the moment into a victory. The person had asked a reasonable practical question. June's calm answer showed how far the production had moved from the night when a clean printed page could silently decide everyone's place.
paragraphs.zh: 開門前，一位來賓問君是否保留贊助商座位。君展示座位表：保留的是無障礙需求與受邀參與者的位置，沒有前贊助商的私人席區。她提供和其他人相同的可選座位。瑪拉聽見，忍住把這一刻當成勝利的衝動。對方只是合理詢問實際安排。君平靜的回答，顯示製作已走離那個讓乾淨印本默默決定所有人位置的夜晚。

paragraphs.en: On opening night, the school hall filled slowly. The tickets were optional, and the first rows stayed clear for those who needed easier access. June counted everyone at the door. Theo lit the stage only after the exits had been checked.
paragraphs.zh: 首演當晚，學校禮堂漸漸坐滿。票價採自願制，前排保留給需要方便進出的人。君在門口清點人數；提歐確認出口後才點亮舞台。

paragraphs.en: Nia performed the mother's speech with Ada's chosen words. She did not shout. When she asked why a warning had failed to reach people by the river, the room stayed silent long enough for the question to be heard without pretending the answer was settled.
paragraphs.zh: 妮雅用艾達親自選定的文字演母親。她沒有喊叫。當她問為何警告沒有傳到河邊居民耳中時，全場沉默良久，讓問題被聽見，也沒有假裝答案已經確定。

paragraphs.en: When Nia reached the mother's last question, Mara saw Ada watching from the first row. Ada did not cry. She held the program with both hands and listened. After the silence, the audience applauded without being told which person to hate. Mara felt that the scene had finally found its proper weight.
paragraphs.zh: 妮雅念出母親最後的問題時，瑪拉看見艾達坐在前排。她沒有哭，只用雙手握著節目單安靜聽。沉默之後，觀眾鼓掌，沒有人被指示該恨誰。瑪拉覺得這場戲終於有了合宜的重量。

questions.question: Where does the company rehearse after the rain?
questions.explanation: 下雨後劇團依備案轉到學校禮堂。

questions.question: What does Nia discover without music?
questions.explanation: 妮雅發現不配樂的停頓也有力量。

title: The Names on the Last Page

paragraphs.en: One month later, the Harbor Lantern Theatre published a version history of the play. Mara's name appeared as playwright, June as stage manager, Theo as lighting designer, and each performer and approved contributor received the credit they had chosen.
paragraphs.zh: 一個月後，港燈劇院公布《河水漲起時》的版本歷程。瑪拉的名字列為劇作家、君是舞台監督、提歐是燈光設計，其他表演者與同意公開的貢獻者，也獲得自己選擇的署名。

paragraphs.en: In the theatre archive, the folder for When the River Rose had room for future corrections. Mara checked that Rina's withdrawn passages were not included in public copies. The original private materials remained protected; the version history showed decisions without exposing the people who had trusted them.
paragraphs.zh: 劇院檔案室裡，《河水漲起時》的資料夾留有未來修正的空間。瑪拉確認莉娜撤回的段落沒有出現在公開版本。原始私密材料受到保護，版本歷程則記錄決定，而不暴露信任他們的人。

paragraphs.en: The records distinguished interview facts from dramatic inventions and kept private material closed. Celeste completed her transition and left with a written account of her changes. The company could not claim every conflict had disappeared, but it had rules for future edits.
paragraphs.zh: 紀錄清楚區分訪談事實與戲劇虛構，私密材料仍封存。席莉絲完成交接，留下修改工作的書面說明。劇團無法宣稱所有衝突都消失，卻為未來修訂建立了規則。

paragraphs.en: Outside, a small agriculture fair displayed a cart of fresh crop beside the entrance. A cleaner moved a heap of leaves, then rubbed a tired heel. The educational stall showed how an efficient garden could provide plenty of food for a neighborhood. A student drew a rectangle around a map of the community’s location. Another explained that raw vegetables would shrink after cooking, while a cook offered a thin slice of bread. Children laughed at harmless gossip about a visiting musician, and Mara reminded them to be kind. A vendor said that some plants suck water through their roots and that gardeners must tend them patiently. The lobby grew full of people from different parts of the city. No one had to pass through a narrow tunnel to find a seat; volunteers had prepared clear paths. Mara saw an innocent child asking where the music would come from. “From all of us,” she said, “but each person’s name still matters.”
paragraphs.zh: 入口旁的小型農業展擺著一車新收的作物。清潔員移開一堆落葉，揉揉疲累的腳跟。教育攤位解說高效率菜園如何為社區提供充足食物。學生在社區位置地圖周圍畫一個長方形。另一人解釋生蔬菜烹調後會縮小，廚師則提供薄麵包片。孩子們笑談來訪音樂家的無害閒話，瑪拉提醒要厚道。攤販說，有些植物透過根部吸水，園丁必須耐心照料。大廳逐漸聚滿城市各處的人。志工已安排清楚動線，沒人需要穿過狹窄隧道才能找到座位。瑪拉看見一名天真孩子問音樂從哪裡來。「從我們每個人這裡來，」她說，「但每個人的名字仍很重要。」

paragraphs.en: Theo sent Mara a message from his new workplace, asking whether the next play still had a place for light. Mara replied that it had many places, but no finished plan yet. They agreed to meet for dinner without turning the evening into another rehearsal. Their story was allowed to continue beyond the curtain.
paragraphs.zh: 提歐從新工作地點傳訊息，問下一齣戲是否還有燈光的位置。瑪拉回答，有很多位置，但計畫尚未完成。他們約好吃晚飯，不把那晚變成另一次彩排。兩人的故事可以在幕後繼續。

paragraphs.en: A community committee secured modest support for another season. Mara began writing a new play about a town that chose to listen before answering. Theo accepted a full-time job with another theatre; they agreed to keep meeting when their schedules allowed.
paragraphs.zh: 社區委員會取得足以支撐下一季的基本資金。瑪拉開始寫一齣關於小鎮先傾聽再回答的新戲。提歐接受另一間劇院的全職工作；兩人約定有空時繼續見面。

paragraphs.en: After the final reading, Mara helped June return the borrowed chairs. On the last seat lay a program with a note from Ada: the doorway was right this time. Mara read it twice before asking whether the note could be kept privately with the rehearsal record. Ada agreed to that use alone. Mara placed it inside a plain envelope. She did not need to print the compliment or turn it into an advertisement. Outside, Theo waited with two cups of tea. Mara joined him, carrying neither a speech nor a new set of instructions, and they walked toward dinner.
paragraphs.zh: 最後讀劇後，瑪拉幫君歸還借來的椅子。最後一張座位上有節目單，艾達留下字條：這次門口的位置對了。瑪拉讀了兩遍，才問能否把字條私下保存在排練紀錄。艾達只同意這一用途。瑪拉把它放進普通信封，不必印出讚美，也不必做成廣告。外面，提歐拿著兩杯茶等她。她沒帶演說或新指示，和他一起走去吃晚飯。

paragraphs.en: At the final reading, Nia held up the restored page and asked Mara whether she wanted to read the mother's words herself. Mara shook her head. Those words had found their speaker. She chose to remain in the audience and listen.
paragraphs.zh: 最後一次讀劇，妮雅舉起恢復的那頁，問瑪拉是否要親自念母親的話。瑪拉搖頭。那些話已找到自己的說話者；她選擇留在觀眾席傾聽。

questions.question: What does the theatre publish later?
options: A version history and proper credits
questions.explanation: 劇院公布清楚的版本歷程與合宜署名。

questions.question: What do Mara and Theo choose?
options: To keep meeting while working separately
questions.explanation: 兩人保有各自工作，也願繼續來往。
